channel.title: The Margin Wars | The Rulebook Wire [Preview]
channel.description: Preview, pending Avi’s review — official sources, practical moves.

item.title: Canada: RTR launch set for 9 November
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Check provider readiness for the scheduled RTR launch, not assumed availability. Preview, pending Avi’s review. Payments Canada confirms a scheduled 9 November launch. This preview does not describe the service as already live. Who: Canadian banks, PSPs and payment users. Effective: 2026-11-09. Official source: https://www.payments.ca/canadas-real-time-rail-launch-confirmed-budget-2026

item.title: EU PSR: Council first-reading position
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Track the EU legislative process; this milestone is not an application date. Preview, pending Avi’s review. The Council voting record documents adoption of its first-reading position on 29 October. This is a legislative milestone, not an application date. PSD3 and PSR must be tracked separately; no implementation date is asserted here. Who: EU payment providers; not automatically UK firms. Effective: Not confirmed / not applicable. Official source: https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15154-2026-INIT/en/pdf

item.title: PSD3: a separate Council milestone
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Track PSD3 separately from PSR; do not treat this vote as a go-live date. Preview, pending Avi’s review. The Council voting record documents its first-reading position on the payment and electronic-money services directive on 29 October. This is not an implementation deadline. Who: EU payment and e-money institutions; not automatically UK firms. Effective: Not confirmed / not applicable. Official source: https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15152-2026-INIT/en/pdf

item.title: NZ moves on commercial cards
item.description: [cost down] So what for merchants: Lower regulated commercial-card interchange is coming; confirm what your acquirer passes through. Preview, pending Avi’s review. The 22 October decision introduces commercial credit-card interchange limits on Mastercard and Visa. Who: New Zealand merchants and acquirers. Effective: 2027-04-22. Official source: https://www.comcom.govt.nz/regulated-industries/projects/interchange-fee-regulation/

item.title: Pix DICT: refund monitoring default
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Check refund integrations that rely on implicit monitoring defaults. Preview, pending Avi’s review. DICT 2.13.0 changes the default value of Refund MonitorAccount to false. Review integrations for implicit defaults. Who: Pix participants and refund engineering teams. Effective: Not confirmed / not applicable. Official source: https://www.bcb.gov.br/content/estabilidadefinanceira/pix/changelog.html

item.title: 3DS 2.4: draft, not a mandate
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Watch the 3DS draft; do not schedule a mandatory migration on this source alone. Preview, pending Avi’s review. EMVCo reports that draft Protocol and Core Functions v2.4 is available for Associate and Subscriber review. No global migration deadline is asserted. Who: 3DS servers, SDK providers and authentication teams. Effective: Not confirmed / not applicable. Official source: https://www.emvco.com/news-publications/emvco-newsletter-q3-2026/

item.title: Scheme fees come into view
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Use the new scheme-fee disclosures to challenge unexplained line items. Preview, pending Avi’s review. First quarterly aggregate fee publications by designated card networks were due for the July–September period. Who: Card networks; acquiring teams. Effective: 2026-10-30. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Acquirer fee disclosures begin
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Compare published acquirer fees with your own card mix and contract. Preview, pending Avi’s review. Qualifying large acquirers must publish merchant service fee data by merchant size and card type. Who: Large acquirers and merchants. Effective: 2026-10-30. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: UK scheme pricing: evidence required
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Ask for evidence behind relevant UK scheme-fee decisions, not a savings promise. Preview, pending Avi’s review. Relevant scheme-fee decisions must comply with the PSR’s pricing-governance direction from the end of November. Who: Visa, Mastercard and UK acquirers. Effective: 2026-11-30. Official source: https://www.psr.org.uk/publications/policy-statements/ps261-market-review-of-card-scheme-and-processing-fees-final-decision-information-transparency-and-complexity-remedy-pricing-governance-remedy/

item.title: Canada–EU: interlink work supported
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Keep the proposed connection on your roadmap, not your live-route inventory. Preview, pending Avi’s review. A joint commitment supports work toward connecting instant payment systems. It is not an operating cross-border route. Who: Cross-border product and treasury teams. Effective: Not confirmed / not applicable. Official source: https://www.payments.ca/payments-canada-welcomes-joint-canada-eu-commitment-interlink-real-time-payment-systems

item.title: Australia: card surcharge reset
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Recheck checkout pricing: designated card-network surcharge rules changed. Preview, pending Avi’s review. eftpos, Mastercard and Visa no-surcharge rules apply from 1 October after the RBA removed its prohibition on those rules. Who: Australian merchants and acquirers. Effective: 2026-10-01. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/faqs/index.html

item.title: Domestic interchange: lower caps
item.description: [cost down] So what for merchants: Lower domestic interchange caps make pass-through worth checking; net merchant savings depend on your terms. Preview, pending Avi’s review. Revised interchange regulation applies to domestic-issued card transactions acquired in Australia. Who: Australian acquirers and issuers. Effective: 2026-10-01. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Issuer compensation rules change
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Check issuer incentives against the amended compensation rules. Preview, pending Avi’s review. The amended net-compensation regime starts, with transitional arrangements for 2026/27. Who: Card networks and issuers. Effective: 2026-10-01. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Next: prove interchange pass-through
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Ask your acquirer how the interchange reduction reached your statement. Preview, pending Avi’s review. First publication of large acquirers’ interchange pass-through measures covers October–December 2026. Who: Large acquirers and merchant finance teams. Effective: 2027-01-30. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Foreign-issued cards get a cap
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Review foreign-card pricing before the new caps apply. Preview, pending Avi’s review. Interchange caps extend to foreign-issued card transactions acquired in Australia. Who: Cross-border acquiring teams. Effective: 2027-04-01. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Merchant statements get sharper
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Make sure the new statement detail reaches your reconciliation process. Preview, pending Avi’s review. More statement detail is required from the first full statement period starting on or after 1 April. Who: Australian acquirers and merchants. Effective: 2027-04-01. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Scheme-fee roadmap expected
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Watch for the fee roadmap; it is not itself a price cap. Preview, pending Avi’s review. The RBA expects a scheme-fee roadmap by 1 April; this is an expectation, not a new fee cap. Who: Card networks and acquiring teams. Effective: 2027-04-01. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Same Day ACH: $10 million limit
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Check whether the larger Same Day ACH limit changes your payout routing. Preview, pending Avi’s review. Nacha lists an increase of the Same Day ACH dollar limit to $10 million for 17 September 2027. Who: US treasury, payout and originating-bank teams. Effective: 2027-09-17. Official source: https://www.nacha.org/content/summary-upcoming-rule-changes

item.title: ACH credits: 9am availability
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Check payout promises against the receiving bank’s 9am availability duty. Preview, pending Avi’s review. Non-Same Day ACH credits must be available by 9am in the receiving bank’s local time on settlement date. Who: Receiving banks and payout teams. Effective: 2026-09-18. Official source: https://www.nacha.org/rules/funds-availability-requirements-non-same-day-credit-entries

item.title: ACH: IAT definition changes
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Review how your ACH provider classifies international entries. Preview, pending Avi’s review. Nacha lists its revised definition of International ACH Transactions among the September changes. Who: ACH originators and compliance teams. Effective: 2026-09-18. Official source: https://www.nacha.org/content/summary-upcoming-rule-changes

item.title: ACH availability exceptions update
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Ask your bank which availability exceptions affect your credits. Preview, pending Avi’s review. Nacha lists changes to funds-availability exceptions for Non-Same Day credit entries. Check the rule text before changing controls. Who: Receiving banks. Effective: 2026-09-18. Official source: https://www.nacha.org/content/summary-upcoming-rule-changes

item.title: IAT: optional date-of-birth field
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Check how your IAT integration will handle the optional date-of-birth field. Preview, pending Avi’s review. Nacha lists the optional date-of-birth field for IAT entries for 19 March 2027. Who: IAT originators, banks and service providers. Effective: 2027-03-19. Official source: https://www.nacha.org/content/summary-upcoming-rule-changes

item.title: ACH: register IAT contacts
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Confirm ownership of IAT contact registration with your ACH provider. Preview, pending Avi’s review. Registration of IAT contacts in the ACH Contact Registry is listed for 1 January 2027. Who: ACH participants handling international entries. Effective: 2027-01-01. Official source: https://www.nacha.org/content/summary-upcoming-rule-changes

item.title: UK fee transparency: next stage
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Prepare to reconcile fee triggers with acquiring invoices. Preview, pending Avi’s review. Substantive information, transparency and complexity requirements apply from the end of July 2027, subject to the limited fee-logic extension. Who: Visa, Mastercard and UK acquirers. Effective: 2027-07-30. Official source: https://www.psr.org.uk/publications/policy-statements/ps261-market-review-of-card-scheme-and-processing-fees-final-decision-information-transparency-and-complexity-remedy-pricing-governance-remedy/

item.title: Small fee lines: a limited extension
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Some fee logic arrives later; acquirers can request it during the extension. Preview, pending Avi’s review. ITC Standard B is deferred for qualifying fee lines generating £850,000 or less in annual UK gross revenue. During the extension, acquirers can request that information without charge. Who: UK acquirers and scheme billing teams. Effective: 2029-07-30. Official source: https://www.psr.org.uk/media/nqoettxg/ps26-1-sp-fees-market-review-extensions-decision-aug-2026.pdf

item.title: Safeguarding: the operating baseline
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Check how your provider reconciles and safeguards customer funds. Preview, pending Avi’s review. Daily reconciliations, monthly reports and resolution packs form part of the strengthened safeguarding regime. Audit requirements have exceptions. Who: UK payment and e-money firms. Effective: 2026-05-07. Official source: https://www.fca.org.uk/firms/emi-payment-institutions-safeguarding-requirements

item.title: CHAPS: November release deferred
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Remove the superseded November release from your implementation plan. Preview, pending Avi’s review. The Bank of England deferred its entire November 2026 RTGS standards release. This notice does not establish a replacement deadline. Who: CHAPS and RTGS participants. Effective: Not confirmed / not applicable. Official source: https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/news/2026/august/delay-to-the-november-2026-rtgs-standards-release

item.title: Pix DICT: recovery API clarifications
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Review recovery API changes before implementation; a candidate release is not a deadline. Preview, pending Avi’s review. The September release candidate adds FundsRecoveryId path-parameter documentation and clarifies refund-request restrictions. A release candidate is not a compliance deadline. Who: Pix participants and fraud operations. Effective: Not confirmed / not applicable. Official source: https://www.bcb.gov.br/content/estabilidadefinanceira/pix/changelog.html

item.title: 3DS approvals: conditional extension
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Ask your 3DS provider whether its product qualifies for the extension. Preview, pending Avi’s review. EMVCo’s Q3 update reports conditional approval extensions for eligible products intending to migrate to v2.4.0.0. Confirm product-specific eligibility. Who: 3DS product providers. Effective: Not confirmed / not applicable. Official source: https://www.emvco.com/news-publications/emvco-newsletter-q3-2026/

item.title: Agentic payments: intent framework draft
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Separate consumer-intent design work from deployed network requirements. Preview, pending Avi’s review. EMVCo’s draft framework introduces Intent Services for consumer-authorised intent. It is a specification-development step, not a deployed network mandate. Who: Agentic checkout and payment product teams. Effective: Not confirmed / not applicable. Official source: https://www.emvco.com/news-publications/emvco-newsletter-q3-2026/

item.title: Reg II: proposal watch, not a new rate
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Monitor the official docket; do not price a new debit cap from this preview. Preview, pending Avi’s review. The Federal Reserve proposal docket is the source to monitor. No final rate, litigation outcome or effective date is asserted in this preview. Who: US debit economics and regulatory teams. Effective: Not confirmed / not applicable. Official source: https://www.federalreserve.gov/apps/proposals/FR-0000-0095-01/details
